title: Freelancer Workspace — guide
overview: A modular workspace for independent work. Opportunities is available; Finances and AI site creation are future modules.
usage: Sign in and start in New York Flatiron / NoMad. Use a district shortcut for the US, Canada, Ireland or the Netherlands; the map pans and clears stale results without issuing a paid search. Then search explicitly. You can still edit the circle center and radius. Prepare a contact message in English (default) or Brazilian Portuguese independently of the workspace locale. Portfolio is optional; empty values omit its paragraph. Enable the preview option only when you already have a preview, and provide its HTTPS URL. Changes to language, portfolio or preview refresh the editable draft. Opening WhatsApp never records contact automatically.
eligibility: Only companies without a website URL listed by the source are eligible. This is not evidence that a business has no website. Google Nearby Search returns at most 20 ranked places per request; results are non-exhaustive. WhatsApp and Instagram are not inferred from phone numbers. Demo contacts are never opened.
architecture: The browser calls authenticated Next.js Experience routes. A process-api repository adapter forwards the verified session to the Fastify Process API. Domain usecases enforce eligibility; repository adapters isolate memory or Firestore persistence. Firebase SDKs are isolated inside infrastructure.
domains: Opportunity searches use a validated Region value object. Contact state transitions from not-contacted version 0 to contacted version 1. Firebase identity owns each contact record. Contact commands require an expected version and UUID idempotency key. The same command replays its result; conflicting payloads or versions return 409. External provider calls do not occur inside database transactions.
content: English and Brazilian Portuguese UI copy is stored in apps/docs/content/<locale>/workspace.json, accessed through GetContent and the CMS port. Theme tokens come from .stitch/DESIGN.md; separate components live in packages/design-system.
api: POST /api/opportunities/search → POST /v1/opportunities/search; GET /api/opportunities/:id → GET /v1/opportunities/:id; POST /api/contacts → POST /v1/contacts. JSON bodies are validated with Zod. /api/auth/session and /api/auth/logout establish or clear HttpOnly sessions with same-origin checks. GET /api/health is public and contains no user data. Process Swagger: http://localhost:3011/docs; contract: /docs/json. POST /api/site-requests → POST /v1/site-requests accepts {companyId, language: en|pt-BR, brief: up to 2000 characters, idempotencyKey: UUID}, returns 202 with the pending record. GET /api/site-requests/:id → GET /v1/site-requests/:id returns the owner’s record or null (200). Mutations check same origin and verified sessions; Process API authenticates both routes.
configuration: infra.auth.provider: local (development) | firebase-auth (production). infra.repositories.provider: process-api for Next.js; memory (development) | firestore for API. infra.places.provider: demo | google-places. infra.maps.provider: schematic | google. infra.cms.provider: json. domains.opportunities.usecases.search/details/recordContact: default. domains.auth.usecases.session: default. domains.content.usecases.getContent: default. http.swagger.enabled: true. Secrets are environment references; unknown shift keys fail. APP_ENV selects config overrides. infra.queue.provider: local-sqlite (development, durable .data/site-requests.sqlite) | firestore-pending (production, freela-c8c75). This stores pending requests only; firebase-tasks dispatch is deferred with the AI backend. domains.sites.usecases.request/get: default. Production rejects local-sqlite. No theme or design-system token changes.
setup: Target Firebase project freela-c8c75. Google sign-in selected; each user owns their history. The default Firestore Standard Native database is created in us-central1 (Iowa), provider-verified freeTier=true, with deny-all browser rules deployed. The user prioritized cheapest/free hosting; paid recovery features are disabled, and future API runtime is configured in the same region. Billing is enabled and Firebase Authentication is now initialized. Required runtime/App Hosting/Maps/Places/IAM APIs are enabled. The Google provider is still missing its OAuth client; ADC, restricted Maps/Places credentials, App Hosting and CI setup remain pending; see deploy/SETUP.md.
privacy: Only place identifiers and user-entered contact state/history, site-request language and brief are persisted for live Google results; returned company details are not stored in Firestore. Do not put personal contact notes into logs. Local authentication, in-memory contacts and local SQLite queue refuse production startup. App Check and deployment access protection remain required before publishing.
validation: Run pnpm ci:quality and pnpm changelog. Coverage reports are generated per app and the changed-file gate requires 90% in every metric. Queue adapter contracts test replay, owner separation, persistence, duplicates and conflicts. Firestore emulator tests cover concurrent queue submissions and deny-all browser access. Playwright covers international jumps, independent message language, optional URLs and persisted pending requests; Storybook includes preset states and queue states. Local servers: web 3000, API/Swagger 3011, docs 3002, Storybook 6006. There is no running AI listener in this request-capture stage.
verification: International prospecting validation is recorded in docs/international-prospecting.md. Cloud deployment, live Google sign-in and live Places remain subject to the setup prerequisites in deploy/SETUP.md.
deployment: Source publication completed to https://github.com/bruno-bert/freela on November 16, 2026. Application source commit b56e63cab1942c536c2399b6937991a0e73c95a9 has a verified tree identical to the prepared local source, including all Stitch assets. Billing is now enabled and Auth was initialized successfully. Enabling the Google provider through REST returned HTTP 400: INVALID_CONFIG: client_id cannot be empty. Enable Google in https://console.firebase.google.com/project/freela-c8c75/authentication/providers and select the support email so Firebase can provision the OAuth web client. No credentials should be pasted into chat. Google sign-in, restricted Maps/Places credentials and the production application deployment remain pending. See deploy/SETUP.md for evidence and prerequisites.
international: Eight editable search starting points: New York Flatiron / NoMad, Austin South Congress, Toronto Queen West, Vancouver Mount Pleasant, Dublin Creative Quarter, Cork Oliver Plunkett Street, Amsterdam De Pijp and Rotterdam Witte de With. Approximate centers and 1–1.5 km radii target commercial areas documented by official district/tourism guides. These are prospecting suggestions, not evidence that businesses lack websites or will buy. Source links are available beside the selected district; the catalog and citations are documented in docs/international-prospecting.md. Country selection does not determine payment currency; agree USD or another currency with each client. The finance module remains deferred.
siteRequests: In Prepare contact, use Queue website request, optionally add a brief, and choose the intended language. The saved request remains pending, including after reopening the drawer or restarting the local API. Each authenticated user owns their backlog. This is only request capture, explicitly requested without the AI backend: there is no generator, worker, automatic publishing, task dispatch or claim that a site was created. Requesting a site does not record contact and does not enable the already-have-preview option.
siteRequestArchitecture: Sites domain: RequestSite and GetSiteRequest usecases, SiteRequestQueuePort and SitesFactory in Process API. The authenticated Experience API forwards through its SitesPort/process-api adapter and own usecases/factory. Contract schemaVersion=1 contains companyId, language, user-entered brief, status=pending, version=0, createdAt and deterministic request ID; it stores no returned Google business details. Local SQLite opens/closes a connection per operation and uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE; production Firestore uses request-scoped transactions. One pending request per owner/company; exact retries replay their result, equivalent new keys deduplicate, conflicting payloads or key reuse return 409. No side effects occur in transaction callbacks. A future AI implementation must add a separate Cloud Tasks listener with bounded retries and failed-job recovery before dispatch is enabled.
